Application Materials.content:
For the application, applicants should gather supporting documents; some students may need to request documents such as transcripts from their university. Required/application materials include:
- Transcripts and certificates of any essential qualifications.
- Referee details.
- A personal statement, if applicable to the chosen course.
- Queen’s student ID if the applicant is a current / former student.
- **If you have completed your qualification, you should upload your degree award certificate and degree transcript. If you have not yet completed your degree, please upload your transcript to show results to date.**
For **International Applicants**, the University says applications may not be decided until all relevant documents are received, and applicants should upload good quality scanned copies of:
- Degree transcripts for all completed periods of study, undergraduate level and above.
- If the degree is still in progress, a transcript of results achieved to date.
- Copies of official Degree/Diploma Certificates for qualification(s) already completed.
- Certified translations if original documents are not in English.
For references: for all Postgraduate Taught and Research applications, applicants must include the names and contact details of **two referees**, normally academics familiar with undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies. If the applicant has taken a higher degree or postgraduate course recently, one referee should be from that institution. If the applicant has been away from higher education for some time, an employer may be used as one referee. Reference letters do not need to be included with the application; they will be requested directly by the University if required.

Application Deadlines.content:
Due to the popularity of this programme, applicants are advised to apply as early as possible, and ideally no later than **30th June** for courses which commence in **mid/late September**.
Please note the closing date for MSc Data Analytics for **September 2026 entry is 30 June**. Applications received after this date and time will be regarded as LATE and will be considered only if vacancies exist when all applications received by this date and time have been processed.
In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on course finder.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Normally a **2.1 Honours degree** in **Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Computer Applications, or a closely related discipline**, or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University.
- Applicants with a **minimum 2.2 Honours degree in a cognate discipline**, a **2.1 Honours degree in a non-cognate discipline**, or who have not yet completed their degree, will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
- All applicants will be expected to have **significant mathematical ability** for this course. Although there will be no requirement to take an aptitude test, the level of mathematical ability required is indicated at: https://www.admissionstesting.org/for-test-takers/test-of-mathematics-for-university-admission/preparation/
- Applications may be considered from those who do not meet the above requirements but can provide evidence of recent relevant technical experience in industry, for example, in **programming, data analytics, or AI development**. The University's Recognition of Prior Learning Policy provides guidance on the assessment of experiential learning (RPEL).
- For applicants from China Mainland: applicants should hold a good **four-year bachelor degree** from a recognised, well ranked university with an average grade of at least **70-85%**.
| Type of institution | UK 2.1 Hons standard | UK 2.2 Hons with 55% standard | UK 2.2 Hons standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | Final average **75%** | Final average **72.5%** | Final average **70%** |
| Tier 2 | Final average **80%** | Final average **77.5%** | Final average **75%** |
| Tier 3 | Final average **85%** | Final average **82.5%** | Final average **80%** |
**Tier 1:** Prestigious Universities (Double First Class Universities and Top 100 Academic Ranking of World Universities). **Tier 2:** Other Recognised Universities and Independent Colleges affiliated to a Tier 1 Institution (as defined by Queen's). **Tier 3:** Other Independent Colleges recognised by Ministry of Education and Self-Study Degrees.
For many postgraduate taught programmes which require a UK 2:1 standard, Chinese graduates will normally be accepted with a final average mark of up to **2% below** the condition stated in the official offer letter, assuming that performance in key modules is of an appropriate standard. Where the entry requirements are different, borderline cases will be considered at the discretion of the Academic Selector.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Evidence of an **IELTS score of 6.5, with not less than 5.5 in any component**, or an equivalent qualification acceptable to the University is required. IELTS must be **taken within the last 2 years**.
International students wishing to apply to Queen's University Belfast, and for whom English is not their first language, must be able to demonstrate their proficiency in English. Non-EEA nationals must also satisfy UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) immigration requirements for English language for visa purposes. More information: [www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs](https://www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs).
If you need to improve your English language skills before entering this degree programme, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/data-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers English language courses, including [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/data-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English) and [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/data-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English).

Program Overview.content:
Data Analytics MSc is offered as a postgraduate taught programme with **1 year full-time** or **2 years part-time** attendance. Places available are **58 full-time** and **10 part-time**.
Data Analytics is described as a field of rapid developments, with growing demand for qualified experts able to extract benefit from data. The role of a data scientist overlaps computer science, mathematics, statistics, modelling and analytics, while also requiring problem-solving and communication skills. The diversity of data analytics opens job opportunities in software companies, healthcare, banking, insurance, policing, tech companies, intelligent buildings and customer behaviour analytics.
The programme provides a balanced route to learning through a blend of academic study and lab sessions, with a heavy focus on practical engagement with industry. In the first and second semesters, students study six modules full-time, including opportunities for blended and collaborative learning. In the third semester, students undertake a significant industry based project.
Special features include the Analytics in Action module and industry commitment to provide real data for “Analytathons” and projects. The module offers real-world examples of data analytics presented by industry experts working alongside academics who provide the theory, with provision across many academic disciplines in the University. The Frontiers in Analytics module includes state-of-the-art techniques in analytics, particularly Visual Analytics and Behavioural Analytics.
The course is unique in having been developed from engagement with industry rather than traditional academic subject areas. The key core skills that a data scientist needs have been clearly defined and form the basis for the course. There are no optional modules or choice, as all skills are packaged into each individual to produce the “all rounded” data scientist.
The course comprises six taught modules worth **120 CATS** plus a Summer Industry Based Placement project module worth **60 CATS**. Full-time study consists of the six core taught modules and an Industry Based Project module. Part-time students are normally enrolled for two years, with three taught modules in the first year and the remaining taught modules plus the Industry Based Project module in the second year during the Summer session. Each module consists of lectures/labs, helpdesk sessions and assessments, with background reading and preparation work.
The aim of the programme is to offer a multi-disciplinary education in data analytics that prepares graduates with key knowledge, skills and competencies necessary for employment in analytics and data science positions. It aims to provide comprehensive knowledge of the fundamental principles of statistics and computer science underpinning analytics; advanced knowledge and practical skills in analytics theory and practice; tools and techniques for careers in data analytics and data science; skills in practices, processes, tools and methods applicable to commercial and research analytics contexts; exposure to current software packages and emerging analytics applications; and opportunities to develop practical skills in a commercial context.
People teaching the course include [Dr David Wilkins](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/david-wilkins), [Dr Emanuele Fino](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/emanuele-fino), [Dr Felicity Lamrock](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/felicity-lamrock) as Course Director, [Dr Laura Boyle](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/laura-boyle), [Dr Matt Nicholl](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/matt-nicholl), [Dr Matthew Streeter](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/matthew-streeter), [Dr Salissou Moutari](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/salissou-moutari), and [Prof Adele Marshall](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/adele-marshall).
Assessment includes coursework, written/practical examinations, project dissertation, and presentations. Canvas is used as the University’s Virtual Learning Environment, with module sites containing recorded lectures, readings, video links, useful web links, discussion forums and activities.
Industry forecasts indicate that Data Analytics is a growing field internationally, with job opportunities predicted to grow by **160% between 2013 and 2020** according to the eSkills report, Big Data Analytics 2013-2020. The course is designed to meet industry needs by giving graduates skills and expertise in computer science, mathematics and statistics, plus experience from an individual industry based project. Queen’s postgraduates also benefit from leadership and executive programmes and integration with business experts. The Energia Data Analytics Prize is awarded to the MSc Data Analytics student with the best overall performance.
Course location: [Mathematics and Physics](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/SchoolofMathematicsandPhysics/).

Curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)** or **2 years (Part-time)**. The programme provides a blend of academic study and lab sessions, with practical engagement with industry. In the first and second semesters, full-time students study 6 modules; in the third semester they undertake a significant industry-based project.
The course comprises **six taught modules (120 CATS)** plus a **Summer Industry Based Placement project module (60 CATS)**:
- Data Analytics Fundamentals
- Database & Programming Fundamentals
- Data Mining
- Machine Learning
- Frontiers in Analytics
- Analytics in Action
- PLUS Individual Industry Based Project (Summer)
Full-Time/Part-Time Study Options:
- **Full-time (1 year):** consists of the six core taught modules (**120 CATS points**) and an Industry Based Project module (**60 CATS**).
- **Part-time (2+ years):** part-time students are normally enrolled for two years. The first year will normally comprise three taught modules (**60 CATS**) - Data Analytics Fundamentals, Data Mining and Frontiers in Analytics. The second year normally comprises the remaining three taught modules (**60 CATS**) - Database & Programming Fundamentals, Machine Learning, Analytics in Action PLUS the Industry Based Project module (**60 units**) which will take place during the Summer session (June-September).
Each module will consist of lectures/labs, helpdesk sessions and assessments and will include some background reading and preparation work. Indicative number of modules per semester: 3.
Core Modules:
| Module | Credits | Module Code | Teaching Period | Duration | Core/Optional |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data Analytics Fundamentals | 20 | DSA8001 | Autumn | 12 weeks | Core |
| Database & Programming Fundamentals | 20 | DSA8002 | Autumn | 12 weeks | Core |
| Data Mining | 20 | DSA8003 | Autumn | 12 weeks | Core |
| Machine Learning | 20 | DSA8021 | Spring | 12 weeks | Core |
| Frontiers in Analytics | 20 | DSA8022 | Spring | 12 weeks | Core |
| Analytics in Action | 20 | DSA8023 | Spring | 12 weeks | Core |
| Individual Industry Based Project | 60 | DSA8030 | Autumn | 12 weeks | Core |
Assessments associated with the course include coursework, written/practical examinations, project dissertation, and presentations. There are no optional modules or choice.

Multiple Applications.content:
After you have entered the core details about yourself and your academic background, you can apply for one or multiple courses through the [Queen's Portal](https://go.qub.ac.uk/pgapply).
If you have applied for and been offered a place on more than one programme of study, you must indicate whether you wish to accept or decline the offer against each programme. Given that your final programme choice may be dependent on funding and/or other factors, you may initially decide to accept more than one offer of a place.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Applications for deferred entry may be permitted. However, in considering requests for deferred entry it will be necessary to consider if the course will be offered in a subsequent year or, in the case of research, the research project and/or intended supervisor is available in a subsequent year. Requests will be considered on an individual basis, particularly in relation to non-UK/Irish applicants who may have experienced delays in obtaining an entry visa in time to commence their studies. Applications for deferral of University administered funding are not permitted.

For many postgraduate taught programmes which require a UK 2:1 standard, Chinese graduates will normally be accepted with a final average mark of up to **2% below the condition stated in the official offer letter**, assuming that performance in key modules is of an appropriate standard.”

It is only on receipt of these documents that we will be able to confirm your acceptance.”
